Supplant

/suh-PLANT/ - rhymes with grant · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Supplant means to take the place of another, often by force or scheming.

In three winters the snowmobile supplanted the dog team across the delta, and the kennels went quiet.

Worked Example

The understudy did not wait for luck: she learned the lead's blocking, courted the director at every note session, and by spring had supplanted her on the opening-night card.

Supplant is sharper than replace because it keeps the smell of the maneuver — the lead did not step down or wear out; her place was taken from beneath her, move by patient move.

How Supplant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

oust

oust: force out openly — blunt and immediate

unseat

unseat: remove from an official seat or title

Antonyms

support

support: hold something up rather than push it aside

serve

serve: work loyally under someone, wanting them to keep their place

How Strong Is It? — succeed → supplant → overthrow

succeed vs. supplant

succeed vs. supplant: Succeed is the mild, lawful case — the heir succeeds the founder with everyone's blessing and nobody pushed.

overthrow vs. supplant

overthrow vs. supplant: Overthrow goes further than supplant: not a quiet slide into someone's chair but open force — the palace stormed, not whispered through.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — sup-

Prefix — sup-: under (a form of sub-)

Root — plant

Root — plant: sole of the foot (Latin planta)

Put it together

Put it together: Sup- (under, a form of sub-) + plant (the sole of the foot, Latin planta) = to trip up from beneath — to hook a foot under someone and take the ground they stood on. The anatomical root survives in plantar, the medical word for the sole. The scheming flavor of supplant is original equipment: it has meant winning a place by underhanded footwork for as long as English has had it.

Use the root in a new word: plantar

Use the root in a new word: plantar: Runners with plantar fasciitis feel every mile along the soles of their feet.

Root Check

Word Choice

vivid / narrative

Supplant tells a small story: something held a place, and something else now holds it — often after pushing. Use it for rivals, invasive species, and technologies that shoulder predecessors aside. Supersede, taught in this unit, is the paperwork version, an orderly succession by the newer standard; if the takeover was earned by open force, overthrow or oust says so louder.
